G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd
BRANCH MANAGER
Training Framework  ·  14–20 days at Chandigarh HQ
Structured across three streams — Operations, Sales, Leadership

How This Training Works
Every Branch Manager goes through this program at Chandigarh before being deployed to a new clinic. The program runs 14 to 20 days, depending on the trainee's learning curve. Sign-off comes from every trainer plus a final readiness test — three consecutive days running a Chandigarh shift solo.

Three streams
STREAM 1 — Operations. Reception, housekeeping, therapist coordination, doctor coordination, compliance. Owned by Jaspreet (Chandigarh BM) and Saurabh.
STREAM 2 — Sales. Counsellor work, the playbook, conversion, follow-ups, upsell/cross-sell. Owned by Manisha and the Senior Counsellor at Chandigarh.
STREAM 3 — Leadership. Branch growth planning, P&L, team development, BM-Doctor peer relationship, escalation discipline. Owned by Regional Head + founder.

Sign-off principle
Sign-off requires evidence of competence, plus a final readiness test.  The final test: three consecutive days at Chandigarh where the trainee runs the branch shift solo — Jaspreet steps back, observes from a distance, and the trainee runs reception huddle, counsellor debrief, BM-Doctor meeting, and end-of-day reporting independently. Only when all three days run cleanly is she signed off.

STREAM 1  ·  OPERATIONS

Module 1  ·  Reception Operations
What the BM must be able to do by end of module
Audit the reception team against the 10-item scorecard
Run the reception morning huddle (5 min)
Coach a receptionist on a specific gap in 10 minutes
Identify CRM hygiene issues — missing entries, mistagged leads, missed callbacks

Activities
Day 1: Shadow Jaspreet's reception huddle
Day 2: Co-run the reception huddle, then run it solo with Jaspreet observing
Day 2: Independent reception scorecard exercise — score vs Jaspreet's score, discuss differences

Sign-off criteria
Can run reception huddle independently
Scorecard accuracy within 1 point of Jaspreet's
Has coached at least one receptionist live
Jaspreet confirms readiness

Module 2  ·  Housekeeping & Hygiene
What the BM must be able to do by end of module
Audit housekeeping work end-to-end against the 6-item wall poster standard
Run housekeeping morning huddle in Hindi, in the appropriate register
Coach the housekeeping team without triggering fear or withdrawal
Understand Saurabh's compliance framework and how it ties to branch audits

Activities
Day 1: Walk with Arshpreet through her full hygiene audit
Day 2: Independent hygiene audit vs Arshpreet's findings
Day 2: Observe and then run a housekeeping huddle in Hindi
Day 2: 60 min with Saurabh on compliance framework

Sign-off criteria
Can run independent hygiene audit, findings match Arshpreet within 1 point
Can communicate with housekeeping team in their language and register
Arshpreet + Saurabh confirm readiness

Module 3  ·  Therapist Coordination
What the BM must be able to do by end of module
Audit therapist treatment delivery — cabin prep, machine handling, timer discipline, handoff
Identify therapists rushing sessions, skipping protocols, or providing inconsistent experience
Understand the three operational rules — timer, verbal handoff, cabin log
Coordinate therapist workload with senior doctor (peer relationship in practice)

Activities
Day 1: Shadow 2-3 therapist sessions end-to-end
Day 2: Cabin audit walk with Arshpreet
Day 2: Workload-scheduling exercise with Jaspreet

Sign-off criteria
Can audit therapist delivery independently
Understands the three rules and how they are enforced
Senior Therapist + Jaspreet confirm readiness

Module 4  ·  Doctor Coordination — the Peer Relationship
Critical module.  This is the structural relationship that most BMs in this industry get wrong. Spend the time here even if other modules are signed off faster. A BM who cannot hold a peer relationship with the doctor will damage the branch within months, regardless of how good her operations are.

What the BM must be able to do by end of module
Run the daily BM-Doctor meeting independently — six agenda items
Draft the daily MoM same day, get doctor's agreement, file to corporate
Know clearly what is clinical (escalate to doctor) and what is operational (handle as BM)
Hold the peer line — neither manage the doctor nor be managed by her

Activities
Day 1: Sit in on Jaspreet's daily meeting with the doctor at Chandigarh. Observe agenda, tone, MoM process.
Day 2: Co-run the meeting with Jaspreet
Day 3-4: Run the meeting independently with Jaspreet observing from outside
Day 4: Boundary exercise — 10 scenarios where trainee decides 'clinical' vs 'operational', discussed with Dr Kanikta

Sign-off criteria
Has run at least 3 BM-Doctor meetings independently
MoMs are accurate, filed same day, signed by both parties
Boundary exercise scored correctly — clear understanding of clinical vs operational
Jaspreet + Dr Kanikta + Senior Doctor at Chandigarh confirm readiness

STREAM 2  ·  SALES

Module 5  ·  Counsellor Verification
What the BM must be able to do by end of module
Verify a counsellor consultation against the 6-step playbook
Audit a CRM record and identify inflated promises, missing follow-ups, undocumented details
Audit telephony data and distinguish real follow-ups from dialled-and-dropped calls
Coach a counsellor on a specific gap — objection handling, math, body language
Run the 6 PM counsellor debrief — six questions, 15 minutes

Activities
Day 1: Sit in on 3 live counsellor consultations at Chandigarh
Day 2: CRM audit exercise — 10 records reviewed with senior counsellor
Day 2: Telephony audit exercise — pull a day's call data, identify real vs fake follow-ups
Day 3: Observe Jaspreet running the 6 PM debrief, then run it

Sign-off criteria
Can identify counselling quality issues in a live session
Can run the 6 PM debrief independently
Has run at least one coaching conversation
Senior Counsellor + Jaspreet + Manisha confirm readiness

Module 6  ·  Sales KPIs & The Four Core Numbers
What the BM must be able to do by end of module
Read and interpret the four core sales KPIs — conversion to package, total revenue, overall conversion rate, upsell/cross-sell
Understand the fifth core KPI — follow-up discipline — and why sell-and-hold is core to GLEUHR
Read branch P&L — revenue, costs, contribution margin
Set monthly counsellor targets in agreement with Manisha and individual counsellors
Forecast branch revenue for the next month with defended assumptions

Activities
Day 1: Session with Manisha on the four core KPIs + follow-up discipline
Day 2: Branch P&L analysis exercise — read 6 months of Chandigarh's numbers
Day 2: Target-setting exercise — set realistic targets for a counsellor based on history
Day 3: Forecast exercise — project next month's branch revenue, defend assumptions to Manisha

Sign-off criteria
Can read P&L confidently
Can set realistic branch and counsellor targets
Manisha confirms readiness in writing

STREAM 3  ·  LEADERSHIP

Module 7  ·  Branch Growth Plan
What the BM must be able to do by end of module
Build a monthly Branch Growth Plan covering all six required sections
Distinguish a report (what happened) from a plan (what will happen)
Identify the top 3 issues to eradicate each month with owner, due date, success criteria
Identify the top 3 growth bets each month — specific actions, not aspirations

Activities
Day 1: Read 3 past Branch Growth Plans (real or template) with the Regional Head
Day 2: Draft a Branch Growth Plan for Chandigarh as a practice exercise
Day 2: Present the plan to Regional Head + Manisha + Saurabh; defend it

Sign-off criteria
Plan covers all six sections clearly
Forward-looking, not backward-looking — at least 5 of 6 sections about the next month
RH + Manisha + Saurabh confirm readiness

Module 8  ·  Team Development & Succession
What the BM must be able to do by end of module
Identify an Assistant BM candidate and build their development plan
Coach an underperformer — when to coach, when to escalate, when to exit
Hold a difficult performance conversation without breaking the relationship
Build a team rhythm — daily, weekly, monthly — that produces consistent output

Activities
Day 1: Walk through Chandigarh's team with Jaspreet — who is strong, who is struggling, who is being prepared
Day 2: Role-play a difficult performance conversation with Manisha playing the team member
Day 2: Asst BM identification exercise — apply criteria to Chandigarh, identify one

Sign-off criteria
Can hold a difficult conversation in role-play without breaking
Can identify Asst BM candidate with clear reasoning
Jaspreet + Regional Head confirm readiness

Module 9  ·  Hard-Line Violations & Escalation Discipline
What the BM must be able to do by end of module
Recognise all 8 hard-line violations (from Counsellor Playbook) and know why each is termination-track
Know the escalation chain — BM, RH, Manisha/Saurabh, Harman, Founder
Recognise when a team member is being pressured to break a hard line, and intervene
Hold the line on rules even when revenue is at stake — especially when revenue is at stake

Activities
Day 1: Session with founder or Harman on the 8 hard-line violations — why they exist, what happens when they're broken
Day 2: 10-scenario drill — for each, identify whether it's a hard-line violation and what to do
Day 2: Discussion with Saurabh on past audit findings and what BMs did right or wrong

Sign-off criteria
Can name and explain all 8 hard-line violations from memory
Scores correctly on the 10-scenario drill
Demonstrates willingness to escalate without hesitation
Founder or Harman confirms in writing

Final Test  ·  Three Solo Days at Chandigarh
After all 9 modules are signed off, the trainee runs Chandigarh solo for three consecutive working days. Jaspreet steps back. Regional Head and Manisha observe from a distance. The trainee runs:

Morning floor walks and three huddles (reception, housekeeping, counsellor)
Daily BM-Doctor meeting + MoM filed to corporate
Counsellor consultation observations and CRM audits
6 PM counsellor debrief
End-of-day reporting — WhatsApp summary to RH, daily log filled
Any client issues, team issues, or escalations as they arise

Sign-off — the final test
All three days must run cleanly.  If a day goes wrong, it does not necessarily mean failure — but the trainee re-does that day before deployment. If two of three days have major issues, the trainee returns to weaker modules for additional time. We do not deploy BMs who haven't demonstrated solo readiness.

Final deployment meeting
Manisha + Saurabh + Regional Head + Founder meet the trainee together
Reviews master sign-off sheet
Reviews the three solo days
Branch assignment confirmed
First Branch Growth Plan deadline set (within 30 days of arrival)
